newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht falls on dollar's overseas surge.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht falls on dollar's overseas surge.

text.p: The Thai baht fell sharply against the U.S. dollar on Monday following the Americad the baht/dollar mid-rate at 67-month low of 25.71 on Monday against 25.67 on Friday.
The baht's weakeness against the bullish dollar was significantly limited by steady foreign inflows and strong demand for baht to meet the central bank's bi-weekly reserve required, dealers said.
Banks have to meet central bank reserve requirements on the seventh and 22nd of every month.
"The heavy selling of the dollar today made the U.S. unit trade very low against the central bank's fixing," said one dealer at a foreign bank. "There was continued inflow of foreign funds."
The overnight interbank rate firmed to 12.00-12.50 percent in late trade from 11.50-12.00 in the morning and 10.50-10.75 late on Friday, dealers said.
"The money supply will remain tight until the passing of the central bank's reserve requirement," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
